instagram_caption:
You can't tickle yourself. Your brain spoils the surprise 🪶

When you move, your cerebellum predicts exactly what you're about to feel and turns the feeling down before it arrives. In tickle robot experiments, adding a delay of up to a fifth of a second made people's own tickles feel more tickly.

Someone else's fingers can't be predicted, so you get the full tickle.

Sources: Scientific American (Sarah-Jayne Blakemore), Nature Neuroscience 1998, UCL.
